Clear simtte's compiled-model cache

Source: R/parallel.R
simtte_model_cache_clear.Rd

Removes compiled model artifacts that simtte_prepare_model/ sim_tte_ode built under simtte_model_cache. Only ever removes directories this package itself created (version-qualified subdirectories named exactly like simtte_model_cache's own return value) – never the configured base directory itself, and never anything under mrgsolve's own default tempdir() locations that this package did not create. Safe to call even if simtte.cache_dir happens to be pointed at a directory with other, unrelated content in it (e.g. a user's home directory): only the recognizably-named version subdirectories are ever candidates for removal, and each is double-checked to actually resolve under the configured base before being deleted.

Usage

simtte_model_cache_clear(all = FALSE)

Arguments

all

Logical, default FALSE: remove only the current version-qualified subdirectory – the one simtte_model_cache would return right now. If TRUE, remove every version-qualified subdirectory found under the configured base – useful after an R, simtte, or mrgsolve upgrade, when a persistent simtte.cache_dir has accumulated subdirectories for versions no longer in use.

Value

Character vector of the directory paths actually removed, invisibly (character(0) if there was nothing to remove). A directory that could not be fully removed is left out, with a warning naming it.

Windows

Windows cannot delete a file that is open. The compiled file of a model loaded in the current session (by simtte_prepare_model or sim_tte_ode) stays open while it is loaded (normally until R exits), so its directory survives the clear. Everything else in it is removed, including mrgsolve's cache record, so the next simtte_prepare_model() still rebuilds the model. Restart R and clear again to remove the remainder. Linux and macOS remove the directory completely.

See also

simtte_model_cache, which returns the directory this clears. simtte_prepare_model, which rebuilds a model the next time you call it. sim_tte_ode, which does the same implicitly.

Examples

simtte_model_cache()
#> [1] "/tmp/Rtmpvxnpko/simtte-model-cache/R4.6.2-simtte2.0.0.9000-mrgsolve2.0.1"
simtte_model_cache_clear()
